premise: A historical drama set in 1945 when the mathematician John von Neumann invented the modern computing blueprint.
title: VON NEUMANN · 1945
overview: The research reveals the frantic technical landscape of 1945 where advanced mathematics collided with early electronic computing. John von Neumann worked across elite academic centers and militarized weapons laboratories to formulate the modern architecture of automatic computation. A mid-level military stenographer acts as a bystander observing von Neumann treat global survival as an abstract logic game. The story tracks how abstract calculations were physically documented, classified, and turned into wartime engineering.

boxes.name: INSTITUTIONAL WORKSPACES AND HARDWARE
boxes.description: Archival blueprints, photographs, and equipment manifests document the laboratories and offices at the Institute for Advanced Study and the University of Pennsylvania in 1945.
boxes.rationale: Art department teams must accurately fabricate the early vacuum-tube computing machinery and period academic offices.
boxes.summary: Archival records detail the physical workspaces at the Moore School of Electrical Engineering and the Institute for Advanced Study. Rooms contained large-scale experimental hardware including the ENIAC and plans for the EDVAC. Photographs show inventors J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly assembling dense electronic assemblies and differential analyzers. Engineering manifests preserve the layouts of physical labs where early programmable computing was built.

boxes.name: WARTIME TRANSIT AND SECURITY
boxes.description: Historical records detail train schedules, military checkpoint procedures, travel rationing coupons, and armed courier protocols between Princeton and Los Alamos in 1945.
boxes.rationale: The script requires authentic logistics for scenes depicting von Neumann carrying classified computational reports across the country.
boxes.summary: Historical transportation files document strict travel rules between Princeton and the Los Alamos laboratory in 1945. Armed military couriers accompanied sensitive components and papers on transcontinental trains. Checkpoints and barbed-wire perimeters isolated the residential sections from the technical installations. Government records track commuter passes, travel rationing, and security clearances across these transit corridors.

boxes.name: ELITE ACADEMIC SOCIAL LIFE
boxes.description: Diaries, menus, fabric catalogs, and photographic archives illustrate the evening attire, cocktail habits, and domestic servant dynamics of Princeton faculty households.
boxes.rationale: Costume and casting departments must accurately represent the elevated class markers of refugee European intellectuals and their American hosts.
boxes.summary: Directories, menus, and photographs record faculty domestic life at the Institute for Advanced Study during the war years. Princeton dining clubs and faculty homes adhered to established social rituals and dinner menus. Domestic staff managed households during periods of national rationing. Archival images show the daily routines, social gatherings, and formal attire of elite scholars.

boxes.name: MECHANICAL COMPUTING ACOUSTICS
boxes.description: Audio archives and technical manuals preserve the acoustic signatures of punched-card sorters, teletype machines, cooling fans, and relays operating under heavy load.
boxes.rationale: Sound designers must construct the distinct auditory landscape of mid-century industrial calculation.
boxes.summary: Manuals and technical logs document the mechanical noise generated by data processing machinery. IBM punched-card sorters, accounting machines, and collators ran on motorized feeds and card tracks. Cooling fans and mechanical relays generated constant acoustic signatures during high-load calculations. Technical guides show how operators punched, verified, and sorted high volumes of physical paper cards.

boxes.name: MATHEMATICAL COLLABORATION DIALECT
boxes.description: Correspondence, declassified meeting transcripts, and peer reviews record the specific theoretical jargon and conversational rhythms used by wartime ballistics researchers.
boxes.rationale: Screenwriters must craft historically accurate dialogue that captures high-level mathematical debates of the era.
boxes.summary: Technical reports from the Ballistic Research Laboratory record the specialized dialect used by wartime weapons researchers. Transcripts capture arguments over numerical integration methods and trajectory tables. Ballisticians used precise vocabulary to link mathematical theory to proving ground ammunition tests. Correspondence preserves the collaboration between academic consultants and military ordnance teams.

boxes.name: MILITARY CLASSIFICATION AND INFORMATION CONTROLS
boxes.description: Declassified censorship directives, document stamping procedures, burn-bag protocols, and nondisclosure logs governing theoretical research across wartime defense projects.
boxes.rationale: It directly links the physical workspaces, transport security protocols, conversational constraints among collaborators, and domestic social discretion demanded of scientists in 1945.
boxes.summary: Declassified records outline the classification system enforced across the Manhattan District and related defense projects. Technical reports were controlled through red stamps, nondisclosure agreements, and document registers. Physical burn bags and secure destruction rules prevented the compromise of weapon calculations. Intelligence files recorded over one thousand security leaks investigated during the war period.

The rest of the bomb was trucked to the Trinity Site in a metal container packed inside of a wooden crate and secured in a steel bed covered by a tarpaulin. All of the shipments were escorted by technical couriers, special agents and armed military police.

A punched card sorter is a machine for sorting decks of punched cards .
Sorting was a major activity in most facilities that processed data on punched cards using unit record equipment . The work flow of many processes required decks of cards to be put into some specific order as determined by the data punched in the cards. The same deck might be sorted differently for different processing steps.
A popular family of sorters, the IBM 80 series sorters, sorted input cards into one of 13 pockets depending on the holes punched in a selected column and the sorter's settings.

The volumes record the Manhattan Project's
activities and achievements in research, design, construction, operation, and administration, assembling a vast amount of information in a systematic, readily available form. The Manhattan District History contains extensive annotations, statistical tables, charts, engineering drawings, maps, photographs, and detailed indices.
Only a handful of copies of the history were prepared. The Department of Energy's Office of History and Heritage Resources is custodian of one of these copies.

WWII Atomic Bomb Project Had More Than 1,500 “Leaks” - Federation of American Scientists. 08.21.14 | 3 min read | Text by Steven Aftergood
The Manhattan Project to develop the first atomic bomb during World War II was among the most highly classified and tightly secured programs ever undertaken by the U.S. government.
Nevertheless, it generated more than 1,500 leak investigations involving unauthorized disclosures of classified Project information.
That remarkable fact is noted in the latest declassified volume of the official Manhattan District History ( Volume 14, Intelligence & Security ) that was approved for release and posted online by the Department of Energy last month.
In several respects, the Manhattan Project established the template for secret government programs during the Cold War (and after). It pioneered or refined the practices of compartmentalization of information, “black” budgets, cover and deception to conceal secret facilities, minimal notification to Congress, and more.
But wherever there are national security secrets, it seems that leaks and spies are not far behind.
During the course of the Manhattan Project, counterintelligence agents “handled more than 1,000 general subversive investigations, over 1,500 cases in which classified project information was transmitted to unauthorized persons, approximately 100 suspected espionage cases, and approximately 200 suspected sabotage cases,” according to the newly
declassified history (at pp. S2-3)

prior_art.premise: A historical drama set in 1945 when the mathematician John von Neumann invented the modern computing blueprint.

neighbors.title: To End All War: Oppenheimer & the Atomic Bomb
neighbors.overview: Explore how one man's relentless drive and invention of the atomic bomb changed the nature of war forever, led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people and unleashed mass hysteria.

neighbors.title: The Imitation Game
neighbors.overview: Based on the real life story of legendary cryptanalyst Alan Turing, the film portrays the nail-biting race against time by Turing and his brilliant team of code-breakers at Britain's top-secret Government Code and Cypher School at Bletchley Park, during the darkest days of World War II.

neighbors.title: Oppenheimer
neighbors.overview: The story of J. Robert Oppenheimer's role in the development of the atomic bomb during World War II.

neighbors.title: A Beautiful Mind
neighbors.overview: From the heights of notoriety to the depths of depravity, John Forbes Nash Jr. experiences it all. As a brilliant but socially awkward mathematician, he made a groundbreaking discovery early in his career and stands on the brink of international acclaim. But as the handsome and arrogant Nash accepts secret work in cryptography, he becomes entangled in a mysterious conspiracy. His life takes a nightmarish turn and he soon finds himself on a painful and harrowing journey of self-discovery.

neighbors.title: The Current War
neighbors.overview: Electricity titans Thomas Edison and George Westinghouse compete to create a sustainable system and market it to the American people.

The movie's plot is based on the true story of a group of young computer hackers from Hannover, Germany. In the late 1980s the orphaned Karl Koch invests his heritage in a flat and a home computer. At first he dials up to bulletin boards to discuss conspiracy theories inspired by his favorite novel, R.A. Wilson's "Illuminatus", but soon he and his friend David start breaking into government and military computers. Pepe, one of Karl's rather criminal acquaintances senses that there is money in computer cracking - he travels to east Berlin and tries to contact the KGB.

neighbors.title: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
neighbors.overview: After the insane General Jack D. Ripper initiates a nuclear strike on the Soviet Union, a war room full of politicians, generals and a Russian diplomat all frantically try to stop it.

neighbors.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E.
neighbors.overview: At the height of the Cold War, a mysterious criminal organization plans to use nuclear weapons and technology to upset the fragile balance of power between the United States and Soviet Union. CIA agent Napoleon Solo and KGB agent Illya Kuryakin are forced to put aside their hostilities and work together to stop the evildoers in their tracks. The duo's only lead is the daughter of a missing German scientist, whom they must find soon to prevent a global catastrophe.

neighbors.title: Mayday
neighbors.overview: When a U.S. Navy pilot on a top-secret mission during the Cold War gets trapped behind enemy lines, his only chance at survival is to form an alliance with an eccentric ex-KGB agent.

neighbors.title: Bridge of Spies
neighbors.overview: During the Cold War, the Soviet Union captures U.S. pilot Francis Gary Powers after shooting down his U-2 spy plane. Sentenced to 10 years in prison, Powers' only hope is New York lawyer James Donovan, recruited by a CIA operative to negotiate his release. Donovan boards a plane to Berlin, hoping to win the young man's freedom through a prisoner exchange. If all goes well, the Russians would get Rudolf Abel, the convicted spy who Donovan defended in court.

neighbors.title: The Shape of Water
neighbors.overview: An other-worldly story, set against the backdrop of Cold War era America circa 1962, where a mute janitor working at a lab falls in love with an amphibious man being held captive there and devises a plan to help him escape.

neighbors.title: The Lives of Others
neighbors.overview: In 1984 East Berlin, dedicated Stasi officer Gerd Wiesler begins spying on a famous playwright and his actress-lover Christa-Maria. Wiesler becomes unexpectedly sympathetic to the couple, and faces conflicting loyalties when his superior takes a liking to Christa-Maria.
